scope: Original practice MCQ18 four-option bounded source crosswalk
question: Which of the following is a limitation of a composite development index?

options.B: It is legally binding on states
options.C: It may conceal district disparities and depend on indicator weights

assessment.A: False universal assertion: composite indices are constructed from data; no primary-source basis for never.
assessment.B: False: a statistical index is not inherently legally binding; distinguish index from any separately enacted policy.
assessment.C: Supported by OECD/JRC 2008 handbook's weighting, aggregation, compensability and disaggregation cautions. District disparity is a logically bounded application, not a district-specific empirical claim.
assessment.D: False universal assertion: composite rankings do not by themselves identify causal effects.

source.title: OECD/European Commission JRC Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators (2008)
source.scope: methodological guidance, not direct Telangana district measurements

conclusion: Existing C retained; no manuscript edit justified; author-side bounded crosswalk only.
